Hard cap 90s from seating to delivery. Stars: 90s=5★ · 95s=4★ · 100s=3★ · 105s=2★ · 120s+=1★ (recipe-correct floor).

Order must reach table within 45s for 5-star margin. Each 5s over deducts 1 star (minimum 2 stars if recipe is correct). Broth < 82°C at pass = instant -2 stars regardless of speed.

Emergency 3★ floor: Rich Tonkotsu + Black Mayu + Barikata 15s + thick chashu. Pre-warm Mayu to 60°C. Skip nori if prep behind — temperature beats garnish.

Japanese Ramen Simulator Beginner Guide: Plan Your First Shop Day (2026)

Pre-launch starter guide to Japanese Ramen Simulator: the first-day shop flow from mise en place to counter service, plus solo play with part-time staff. Built from the official Wild Dog trailer and press coverage.

First Shop Day at a Glance

The first-day loopRead the shop layout → prep toppings and stock → boil and strain fresh noodles → paint your menu board → open the doors and work the counter → close out the day.

3 Traps First-Time Owners Fall Into

TRAP 1

Opening the doors before mise en place is done. Once customers sit down there is no pause button — have chashu, toppings, and noodles portioned first.

TRAP 2

Stacking every crew member on one station. Up to six players share one shop, so split cooking, noodles, and counter service into separate roles.

TRAP 3

Ignoring shop safety. The developer confirms thieves and kitchen fires — keep a fire extinguisher within reach during service.

Sources: Official Trailer, Steam Store Page & Press Coverage

The official 46-second announcement trailer is no longer the only footage: the Steam store description embeds seven in-engine gameplay clips of 2.5–6.3 seconds each. Your First Shop Day in 7 Steps

STEP 01

Step 1: Before Opening — Learn the Shop Layout

Before your first customer sits down, walk the whole floor. Counter seats line an L-shaped counter facing an open kitchen, with a back kitchen for broth and prep. Up to six players share this space, so agree on who owns the cooking line, the noodle pot, and the counter before doors open.

📸 Overhead of the whole shop: counter seats, open kitchen, and prep area in one view — the base map for assigning roles.
STEP 02

Step 2: Mise en Place — Prep Toppings and Stock First

Do your prep while the shop is still quiet: slice and portion chashu, green onion, and toppings, and keep your soup base hot. When the first wave walks in, a bowl should need only assembly — not cooking from scratch.

📸 Close-up of a finished bowl: green onion, chili oil, and three slices of chashu, with the whole roast beside it — what finished prep looks like.
STEP 03

Step 3: Handle Fresh Noodles by Hand

The trailer shows the noodle work done by hand: portion fresh noodles into a wire basket, boil, and shake them dry. Noodles set the pace of every bowl — in co-op, keep one owner on the noodle station so timing stays consistent.

📸 First-person view: shaking a wire basket of fresh noodles dry, with wooden boxes of portioned noodles and chashu on the prep table.
STEP 04

Step 4: Paint Your Menu and Recipe Board

The game ships with a full drawing board: brushes, color sliders, and vertical text tools for designing your own shop sign and menu board. Use it — a clear board tells customers what you sell before they even sit down.

📸 The signboard editor: your painted vertical menu and ramen illustration on the left, brush presets and color sliders on the right.
STEP 05

Step 5: Open the Doors — Counter Service Flow

Customers take counter stools and order; you boil, assemble, and slide bowls down the counter. The loop is: take the order, build the bowl, serve it hot, and free the seat for the next guest. In co-op, hand bowls to a teammate instead of running them yourself.

📸 A customer in a blue suit lifting noodles from a chashu, seaweed, and soft-egg bowl — counter service is exactly this loop, one bowl at a time.
STEP 06

Step 6: The Storefront — Signs and Opening Time

Your exterior works too: the wall plaque hangs on "preparing" until you are ready, then flips to greet guests, while the lanterns and street front give the shop its identity. Check the entrance before every shift so passers-by never mistake your shop for closed.

📸 The front of house before opening: the plaque still reads "preparing," a headband-wearing chef waits beside the red lanterns, and a pagoda rises down the street.
STEP 07

Step 7: Playing Solo — Hire Part-Time Staff

You do not need five friends to run this shop: the developer confirms solo owners can hire part-time staff to cover empty stations. In the trailer a full crew streams through the front door with name tags over their heads — online, those are friends; solo, hired help fills the same slots.

📸 At 8 seconds into the trailer: the two-story corner shop hung with red lanterns as named crew members head inside for the opening shift.

The "Open" Sign — Where the Daily Loop Begins (Official In-Engine Clip)

The official in-engine store clip catches the exact moment a shop day starts: a staff member hangs the wooden "open" sign by the entrance while name-tagged customers dash inside (image below). That sign is the start of the core loop — flip the sign, greet the rush, take orders, boil and build bowls, serve, clear, reset the seat, and keep it spinning until close. Two things come before anything else on day one: hang the sign, and get the pots hot.

Yes — online co-op for 1 to 6 players running one ramen shop together, splitting the cooking line, noodle work, and counter service.

Both appear in the official announcement materials: a shuriken-throwing thief targeting the shop, and kitchen fires you put out with a fire extinguisher. Treat them as service-day hazards and keep the extinguisher close.

Unreal Engine 5. It is developed by Wild Dog, a Tokyo studio whose previous title is Keep Digging.

No demo has been announced as of September 29, 2026. Wishlist the game on Steam to catch announcements — this page will be updated if a demo ships.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q1.Why did my broth turn sour (spoilage warning)?

Leaving the stockpot lid off at closing or letting the pot drop below 70°C triggers spoilage. Keep holding temp at 86–92°C and seal the lid tightly at closing.

Q2.Why is my tonkotsu broth watery instead of milky?

Bones were not split sufficiently to expose marrow, or initial heat was too weak. Maintain a 100°C rolling boil during the first 90 minutes to break down bone collagen.

Q3.Can I boil kombu with pork bones together at 100°C?

No. Kombu above 65°C releases bitter alginic acids that drop umami by 15 points. Steep kombu at 60°C for 30 min and remove before bringing bones to a boil.

Q4.Why can’t tare be poured directly into the stockpot?

Boiling tare destroys volatile aromatic esters in soy sauce and flattens fermented miso notes. Always dose 15ml tare individually per bowl.

Q5.What is the exact temperature cutoff for food critics?

Broth must be ≥86°C upon delivery for 5 stars. 82°C–85°C incurs penalties, and below 82°C fails the critic review entirely.

The shops themselves are level-gated from the first minute, beer rolls in around level 5, and level 7 sends a critic you must impress before miso opens. Rishiri Natural Kombu Kelp Prep & Washing Procedure (Pre-Extraction SOP)

  1. Step 1

    Mannitol Wipe (No Rinse)

    Gently wipe white mannitol powder with damp cloth—rinsing washes away 12% glutamate.

  2. Step 2

    Surface Score (Optional)

    Light cross-hatch on dull side accelerates cold soak diffusion by ~18%.

  3. Step 3

    Cold Mizudashi Setup

    10 g kombu per 1 L filtered water; refrigerate 8–12 h in covered vessel.

  4. Step 4

    Pre-Heat Strain

    Remove kombu before liquid hits 70°C; reserve for niban or tsukudani.

Rishiri Natural Kombu Kelp Temperature Curve & Boiling Thresholds

Cold Water Soak (Mizudashi)4°C ~ 10°C
Duration: 8~12 h

Submerge kombu in filtered water overnight; glutamate diffuses without heat—zero alginic acid release.

Gentle Heat Extract60°C ~ 65°C
Duration: 30~45 min

Hold with thermometer; surface should show fine bubbles, never rolling. Remove kombu before 70°C.

Katsuobushi Infusion85°C
Duration: 15~20 min

After kombu removal, raise to 85°C, add thick katsuobushi, steep off-heat 20 min, strain immediately.

⚠ Never boil kombu: alginic acid + calcium = slimy texture and bitter marine note. Wipe white mannitol powder off surface—do not rinse (flavor loss).
